stem: During follow-up of a child initially thought to have chronic gastrointestinal loss, which finding should prompt reconsideration of a simple decreased-loss explanation?

options.text: Head circumference begins crossing centiles downward
Weight is the first parameter to decrease
Weight loss occurs with head circumference spared
Poor growth remains limited to weight

explanation: Head circumference begins crossing centiles downward is the key warning sign. In chronic gastrointestinal loss, weight is usually affected first while head growth is relatively spared; downward crossing of head circumference centiles suggests a different or additional cause and should prompt reassessment.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because downward crossing of head circumference centiles is not typical of a simple decreased-loss pattern and suggests an alternative or additional pathology.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because weight is usually the first parameter affected in chronic gastrointestinal loss, so this supports rather than challenges the explanation.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a maintained head circumference is expected in a simple decreased-loss pattern and does not prompt immediate reconsideration on its own.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because weight loss with head circumference spared is more consistent with chronic gastrointestinal loss.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because poor growth limited to weight is still compatible with a decreased-loss explanation and does not by itself suggest brain growth impairment.
